slides: Welcome back, and now a new topic, overlapping groups. These questions are about two groups of people, or of things. And some members belong to both groups.

slides.say: Overlap questions show up in about half of the real exams. The good news is that they follow a few clear rules. With the right picture, they become quick questions.
Let's start with an example. In a class, some students play music, and some students play a sport. And some students do both.
Let's draw it as two circles. One circle is the students who play music. The other circle is the students who play a sport.
at: Let's draw it as two circles

slides.say: The circles cross each other. The part in the middle is inside both circles. So these students play music, and they also play a sport. We call this part both, or the overlap.
Now the part of the music circle that is outside the sport circle. These students play music, but no sport. We call it music only.
In the same way, inside the sport circle but outside the music circle is sport only. These students play a sport, but no music.
And there's one more group, the students outside both circles. They don't play music, and they don't play a sport. We call them neither.
So two groups give us four regions. Music only, both, sport only, and neither. Every student is in exactly one of these four regions.
at: So two groups give us four regions
Every student is in exactly one

slides.say: Let's see the four regions once more, with something else. In a parking lot, some cars are red, and some cars are electric.
A red electric car is in the middle, both. A red car that runs on gas is red only. A white electric car is electric only.
at: A red car that runs on gas

slides.say: And a white car that runs on gas? It's not red, and it's not electric. So it's neither, outside both circles.
Is there a car with no region? No. Every car is red or not, and electric or not. So every car is in exactly one region.
Now careful, because here's a mistake many students make. Let's put numbers in our class. Ten students play music. Four of them also play a sport.
So where do the ten go? Not all ten go into music only. The four who also play a sport are in the middle, both.
So music only is ten minus four, six.
So the music students means the whole music circle. That's music only plus both. Six plus four is ten.
Let's look at the sport circle too. Say seven students play a sport. Four of them are in both. So sport only is seven minus four, three.
So when a question says seven play a sport, it means the whole sport circle, sport only plus both. It doesn't mean sport only. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next part.
